source.title: Belfast News-Letter, 20 September 1946, p. 3 ("Nominations for county and rural councils")
source.publisher: Belfast News-Letter (via the British Newspaper Archive)
source.check: Read on the page image: the News-Letter's Ballycastle section lists each division with its nominee (no party labels printed; the recorded party is not from this page). The Northern Whig's list of the same day (p. 3), cited before, does not carry this council.

note: Triennial election, polled Thursday 3 October 1946. Fourteen members were returned. Glenariff had two nominations, but Joseph Lynn was returned unopposed after the withdrawal of Alexander Stewart; the other divisions were unopposed. Returned unopposed.
correctionNote: Citation corrected (w19-bna-fix, Nov 2026): the Northern Whig page cited before (20 September 1946, p. 3) has no Ballycastle list; the member is named in the Belfast News-Letter of the same day, p. 3 (page image), which prints no party labels, so Party_As_Printed is cleared (the recorded party is kept). Party (w19-fixes2, 19 Nov 2026): the recorded UUP had no source, since the Belfast News-Letter list of 20 September 1946, p. 3 prints no party labels. Recorded as Nationalist Party, his party in his adjacent returns in this division: his return before, F. M'Carry, N., 1939 (Frank M'Carry, N., 1924-36); his return after, F. M'Caldy 1949, carries no label. Renamed from 'Fairhead' to The Fair Head (19 Nov 2026, w19-tidy, the owner's decision 4 of 19 Nov 2026: a division filed under two spellings takes its official name, and each round keeps the spelling it was filed under as Constituency_Name_As_Printed): the 1911 DED map (Ballycastle Rural District) and the Northern Ireland DED maps of 1921-69 name the DED The Fair Head; the rounds were filed as Fair Head (1924, 1927, 1930, 1933, 1936, 1939, 1949); Fairhead (1946, 1955). This round was filed as 'Fairhead', kept as Constituency_Name_As_Printed; the old address (fairhead) answers with a redirect to this one.
